programme.title: Britain in Focus: A Photographic History

programme.title: The Secret Genius of Plants

programme.title: Deep, Down and Dirty: The Science of Soil
programme.desc: Gardening expert Chris Beardshaw explores where soil comes from, and what it is made of. It is an often misunderstood substance, with people sometimes dismissing it as dirt, so he reveals it as it has never been seen before using specialist microphotography, and highlights what makes it so essential to life. Research shows that humans are pushing this precious resource to its limit, and scientists are battling to find ways of preserving it for the future

programme.desc: Situated north of the Arctic Circle, the Lofoten Islands in Norway are famed for their dramatic mountain landscapes and cod fisheries. Coinneach arrives MacLeod in March during peak cod season, helping to unload the day's catch and observing the stockfish drying process. He works with a local chef to create a fine-dining dish using the wind-dried cod, makes lefse, a traditional flatbread, and harvests seaweed. A dinner of Lofotlam, a globally protected local lamb, rounds off his visit

programme.title: Miann na Maighdinn-mara (Mermaid Tales)
programme.desc: Kate MacLeod, aka The Hebridean Mermaid, explores the hidden gems of the Hebrides, meeting tradition bearers with remarkable stories about the places she loves to visit the most, above and below the water. In this episode she comes across an interesting sea creature, known as a sunfish, which is native to tropical waters, but is likely to have been carried to the islands by the Gulf Stream. Swimming on its side, the sun heats its body and it feeds on jellyfish. She also journeys to Taransay, home of some of the most stunning and unique beaches in the Outer Hebrides. Once a thriving community, the island had three villages, but is now home to deer, seabirds and cattle.

programme.title: Faodail: Found
programme.desc: The Faodail Film Archive, which gathers lost indigenous film collections from the 1930s to the 1980s in the Outer Hebrides, storing the footage for future generations. programme.title: The Great Food Guys
programme.desc: Nick Nairn and Dougie Vipond focus on meat, cooking a rack of Scottish lamb lamb with roast aubergine, with shepherdess Michelle Stephen and farmer and comedian Jim Smith

programme.title: This Farming Life
programme.desc: The Barclays are finding their feet with their new business, which involves buying lambs to fatten up for the butcher. Rachel and Camy, who are one year into their tenancy, set off to market at Lairg to buy more ewes, while Nikki and Ollie find out if their favourite buffalo is pregnant

programme.title: Murder Trial: Death of a Dog Walker
programme.desc: Part two of two. With Brian Low's family desperately seeking justice and answers, the fate of ex-gamekeeper David Campbell hangs in the balance. Witnesses unearth more shocking revelations and the defendant takes the stand before the jury must answer the ultimate question of his guilt. The court is shown dramatic footage from Campbell's custody interview where tempers flared when allegations were put to him, with the prosecution pointing to a guilty man on the ropes, while the defence argue it shows a police force under pressure to get their man

programme.title: David Wilson's Crime Files
programme.desc: The criminologist and guests delve into the psychology of criminals who lead a secret or double life, hiding behind a respectable or constructed front in order to cover up their illegal activities. In a short film, investigative journalist Fiona Walker takes viewers back to 18th-century Edinburgh to tell the infamous tale of Willie Brodie, town councillor by day, criminal mastermind by night

programme.title: Scotcast
programme.desc: Discussion on Scotland's biggest news stories, with Martin Geissler, Laura Miller and Natalie Higgins

programme.title: Icons of Football
programme.desc: Joy McAvoy narrates a profile of former Scotland captain Gary McAllister, charting his up and downs in a career that saw the midfielder play for Motherwell, Leicester City, Leeds United, Coventry City and Liverpool. With contributions from McAllister himself, as well as Steven Gerrard, Gordon Strachan and Ardal O'Hanlon

programme.title: Reporting Scotland: News at Seven
programme.desc: Reports from BBC newsrooms across the country with analysis and discussion on the big stories of the day

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: Brian Cunningham and Kirsty Wilson show how to take cuttings from various garden favourites, including rhododendrons and a range of tender perennials. Brian also revisis his espaliered apple trees for more essential maintenance and Kirsty pays a visit to the new glasshouses in the Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh

programme.title: World Pipe Band Championships
programme.desc: Jackie Bird presents highlights of the competition held on Glasgow Green, with expert commentary on the most important event in the piping calendar

programme.title: Martin Compston's Scottish Fling
programme.desc: The actor and Phil MacHugh travel along the east coast from St Andrews to Aberdeen, challenging expectations by revealing the surprising side of some well-known places. Starting in the home of golf, the duo take to the beach made famous by the movie Chariots of Fire to indulge in a spot of land yachting with brothers Jamie and Guy McKenzie

programme.title: Martin Compston's Scottish Fling
programme.desc: Martin and Phil MacHugh set out on a sporty journey to explore the north of Scotland, beginning at the Little Ferry Circuit in Golspie, home to the North of Scotland Kart Club. They then head to Inverness for lunch at the Alleycat Restaurant, before taking to the pitch with the town's under-17 shinty team

programme.title: Scot Squad
programme.desc: Road cops Singh and McKirdy pull over a couple of Scotland's most celebrated children's entertainers at a set of traffic lights. Elsewhere, officers rake about a hedge to rescue some very public pornography, and jump in an elevator to battle claustrophobia. Starring Jack Docherty and James Allenby-Kirk

programme.title: Edinburgh Unlocked
programme.desc: Mark Nelson presents another selection of the best of the Edinburgh Festival, featuring the pick of the comedy, music, cabaret and theatre from all over the world

programme.title: Jim Smith Live from Perth
programme.desc: The farmer and comedian performs in his home town on the final night of a sell-out tour, telling tales of rural Scottish life to a packed audience

programme.title: Reporting Scotland: News at Seven
programme.desc: Reports from BBC newsrooms across the country with analysis and discussion on the big stories of the day

programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
programme.desc: Will Kirk and Dominic Chinea travel the UK to pick up items for restoring. In Devon they come across Daisy, the oversized fibreglass dairy cow lantern who has been a fixture at Hemyock Light Parade for a decade but is suffering from the effects of time. In Swindon, Dom meets Tulsi, who has a Hindu holy scripture passed down from her grandmother that's so fragile it cannot be opened without further damage being caused. He also meets up with a master craftsman who gives him a few tips on the art of glass cutting

programme.title: Paramedics on Scene
programme.desc: John and Craig of the Special Operations Response Team are called to Glasgow city centre, where a public brawl has broken out on a busy Saturday evening. On the scene, John helps to coordinate the ambulance response, engaging with police to help keep the two factions separate. The next morning, crewmates Jim and Kire are called to a church in the south of the city where a member of the congregation has collapsed, complaining of chest pain

programme.title: Sportscene: Premiership Highlights
programme.desc: Action from the latest matches, featuring Dundee United v Dundee at the CalForth Construction Arena, Hibernian v Kilmarnock at Easter Road and Motherwell v Aberdeen at Fir Park

programme.title: Murder Trial: Death of a Dog Walker
programme.desc: Part two of two. With Brian Low's family desperately seeking justice and answers, the fate of ex-gamekeeper David Campbell hangs in the balance. Witnesses unearth more shocking revelations and the defendant takes the stand before the jury must answer the ultimate question of his guilt. The court is shown dramatic footage from Campbell's custody interview where tempers flared when allegations were put to him, with the prosecution pointing to a guilty man on the ropes, while the defence argue it shows a police force under pressure to get their man

programme.title: City Lights: Pure Dead Brilliant
programme.desc: A celebration of the comedy that captured the spirit of 1980s Scotland, starring Gerard Kelly as a Glasgow bank clerk with dreams of being a best-selling author. The show's creator Bob Black and cast members Elaine C Smith, Jonathan Watson and Dave Anderson reveal their favourite moments and give behind-the-scenes insights, with bittersweet memories of co-stars Kelly and Andy Gray. With contributions from Gayle Telfer Stevens, Jordan Young, Sanjeev Kohli, Damian Barr, Johnny McKnight Kirsty Wark and Paul English

programme.title: City Lights
programme.desc: Glasgow bank clerk Willie Melvin reckons he could be a best-selling author. He's got the ambition, the determination and the typewriter - all he needs is the talent. First episode of the comedy, originally broadcast in 1984, starring Gerard Kelly, with Andy Gray, Jan Wilson, Dave Anderson and Jonathan Watson

programme.title: Paramedics on Scene
programme.desc: Paul and Nicole of the Special Operations Response Team are called after a mobility scooter plunges down a steep embankment. They work closely with fire and rescue to lower a paramedic down by rope to the patient, where he administers vital pain relief. In Edinburgh, crewmates Kevin and Martyn respond to a 999 call from a concerned member of the public after a man is found unconscious in the city centre

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: Brian Cunningham and Kirsty Wilson show how to take cuttings from various garden favourites, including rhododendrons and a range of tender perennials. Brian also revisis his espaliered apple trees for more essential maintenance and Kirsty pays a visit to the new glasshouses in the Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh

programme.title: Race Against the Tide
programme.desc: Iain Stirling challenges seven teams to create seaside-inspired sand sculptures against the ticking clock of the incoming tide, beginning on St Andrews beach. From nostalgic caravans to cheeky seagulls, creativity meets chaos under the watchful eyes of judges Sadie Clayton and Jamie Wardley

programme.title: The Catch Up
programme.desc: A round-up of the day's news

programme.title: Deadly 60
programme.desc: Steve Backshall visits the marshlands of Argentina in search of an anaconda, and goes swimming in piranha-infested waters

programme.title: Deadly 60
programme.desc: Steve Backshall and the crew are in Peru, on the search for elusive giant river otters

programme.title: Top Gear
programme.desc: Jeremy Clarkson and James May travel to Beijing to learn about China's car industry, which has seen great expansion in recent years - but also have a violent encounter with one of the Stig's cousins. Meanwhile, Richard Hammond immerses himself in the world of Nascar at a race in Texas, and the Mercedes-Benz SLS AMG Roadster is wrestled around the test track, emitting serious amounts of noise and smoke in the process. Future host Matt LeBlanc is the Star in a Reasonably Priced Car

programme.title: Mission: Impossible 2
programme.desc: Secret agent Ethan Hunt is sent to find and destroy the only sample of a deadly man-made virus. However, he faces tough opposition in a former spy-turned-criminal mastermind who has already acquired the cure and now wants the pathogen itself. Director John Woo's action thriller sequel, starring Tom Cruise, Dougray Scott, Thandiwe Newton and Anthony Hopkins

programme.title: Mission: Impossible III
programme.desc: Former secret agent Ethan Hunt is called out of retirement when an ex-trainee is taken hostage by a ruthless arms dealer, but when the rescue operation goes wrong, the villain decides to target Hunt's fiancee. Action thriller sequel directed by JJ Abrams, starring Tom Cruise, Philip Seymour Hoffman, Michelle Monaghan, Ving Rhames and Simon Pegg

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Mexico v England. Action from the round-of-16 match, which took place at Mexico City Stadium

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: France v England. Action from the third-place play-off, which took place at Miami Stadium in the USA

programme.title: Man Like Mobeen
programme.desc: After the attack on his best friends and threats against his sister, Mobeen is armed, dangerous and out for revenge. programme.desc: Trevor Nelson presents a celebration of the work of the American singer, songwriter and producer, who died last August, featuring a rich selection from the BBC's archive of performances of his work from over the decades. As one of the legendary trio Holland-Dozier-Holland, Lamont helped create the Motown sound that spread across the globe in the 1960s, setting a new standard in popular songwriting and winning fans like Bob Dylan and the Beatles with songs such as You Keep Me Hanging On, Baby Love, This Old Heart of Mine and Reach Out I'll Be There. This collection features some Dozier's best-loved and most recognisable hits, performed by Motown's Diana Ross & the Supremes, the Four Tops and Martha and the Vandellas, as well as by those who have kept his work alive including Phil Collins, Kylie Minogue, Rod Stewart and Rag'n'Bone Man
